newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Macquarie Bank shares top turnover.
newsitem.headline: Macquarie Bank shares top turnover.

text.p: Shares in Macquarie Bank Ltd topped turnover in early trade on Tuesday with 19.99 million shares or about 13.4 percent of its ordinary capital traded.

The bulk of the trade was in two lines specialled through Macquarie's stockbroking division. One line was of 9.98 million shares at a price of A$7.60 per share and another was of 9.98 million at a price of A$7.78 per share.
Brokers speculated the sellers of the parcel could be UK-based finance group Hill Samuel.

This was later confirmed by Macquarie Bank which said Hill Samuel, the investment bank unit of Lloyds TSB Plc, had sold all its 13.4 percent stake in Macquarie Bank to the Brunei Investment and Commercial Bank (BICB),
BICB is a wholly owned by the government-owned Brunei Investment Agency.

Macquarie said Hill Samuel and BICB had agreed to share equally the bank's interim dividend of 18 cents per share, declared on November 19, with this outcome being achieved by the different prices for the two parcels of shares.
BICB is now Macquarie's largest individual shareholder and would be invited to be represented on the bank's board, Macquarie Bank said.
By 11.30 a.m. (0030 GMT), Macquarie Bank shares were six cents higher at A$8.80 on turnover of 20.02 million shares.
